p: the LORD: This notable sentence was in the beginning used as the foot or tenor of the song, which was often repeated.
redeemed of the LORD say so: As was true in the Jews, so there is not one of God's elect who does not feel his help in their necessity.
Hungry and thirsty: He shows that there is no affliction so grievous out of which God will not deliver us, and also exhorts them who are delivered to be mindful of so great a benefit.

rebelled against the words of God: Then the true way to obey God is to follow his express commandment: also by this all are exhorted to descend into themselves as none are punished but for their sins.
cried unto the LORD in their: He shows that the reason God punishes us extremely is because we can be brought to him by no other means.
gates of brass: When there seems to man's judgment no recovery, but all things are brought to despair, then God chiefly shows his mighty power.
Fools because of their transgression: They who have no fear of God, by his sharp rods are brought to call on him, and so find mercy.
He sent his word: By healing them he declares his good will toward them.
destructions: Meaning their diseases, which had almost brought them to the grave and corruption.
thanksgiving: Praise and confession of God's benefits are the true sacrifices of the godly.
sea in ships: He shows by the sea what care God has over man, for when he delivers them from the great danger of the sea, he delivers them as it were from a thousand deaths.
melted because of trouble: Their fear and danger is so great.
are at their wits' end: When their art and means fail them, they are compelled to confess that only God's providence preserves them.
quiet: Though before every drop seemed to fight one against the other, yet at his command they are as still as if they were frozen.
congregation of the people: This great benefit should not only be considered particularly, but magnified in all places and assemblies.
turneth the wilderness into a standing: For the love that he bears to his Church, he changes the order of nature for their convenience.
increase: Continual increase and yearly.
Again: As God by his providence exalts man, so he also humbles them by afflictions to know themselves.
contempt upon princes: For their wickedness and tyranny he causes the people and subjects to contemn them.
righteous shall see it: They whose faith is lightened by God's spirit, will rejoice to see God's judgments against the wicked and ungodly.
